title: busfactor successor map
description: A list of packages that are no longer maintained, each with a sourced pointer to what people should use instead. One object per (ecosystem, package) pair.

version.description: Format version of this file. Bump the major number when a field changes meaning.

updated.description: Date of the last edit, YYYY-MM-DD.

ecosystem.description: Which package registry the package lives in.

package.description: Exact package name as published on that registry (npm scope included, Go full module path, Packagist vendor/name).

status.description: Why the package should not be relied on anymore. archived = source repository archived; deprecated = the registry or the maintainers say so; unmaintained = maintainers said they stopped or no fix for a long-known problem; abandoned = Packagist 'abandoned' flag or equivalent; sabotaged = a maintainer deliberately broke a release.

successor.description: Name of the package to use instead, on the same registry, or null when there is no single drop-in successor (see notes). For stdlib successors write the module path (e.g. 'errors', 'tomllib', 'std::io::IsTerminal').

successor_kind.description: fork = same code base continued elsewhere; rewrite = different code base, same purpose, similar API; stdlib = the language's standard library now covers it; different-api = you will have to change your code.

since.description: When the status became true, YYYY-MM. Omit if unknown.

sources.description: At least one public URL that supports the status and the successor: registry page, advisory, README, official announcement.

notes.description: One or two plain-English sentences: what happened and what to do. Keep it short.
